2. On December 4, 1973, the respondent filed the aforesaid title suit fir eviction of the appellant from the suit premises on the ground that they required the premises for bonfire use and occupation and that the appellant was a habitual defaulter. The determination of the points involved the consideration of the agreement between the rustics dated May 1, 1973 which showed that the appellant took the premises at a monthly rent of Tk. 1600/- paying an advance of Tk. 19,200/- which was adjustable in two years in monthly installments of Tk. 800/-. The suit was filed within the seventh month after the appellant entered the premises, when fifty percent rent for seventeen months which was paid in advance was still lying in deposit with the respondents. 

 3. In addition to the facts stated above, the written statement filed by the appellant showed that the appellant invested a huge amount in the hotel business which he started in the premises, purchased various furniture, articles, utensils, crockeries etc., both from the respondent who himself was running a hotel business in the premises and also from outside, that he employed a large number of workers and had obtained a license for running his hotel business in the premises, that the respondents were demanding salami or 25% shares in the hotel business and on his refusal to comply with their illegal demand the respondents threatened to evict him for the premises and refused to accept the rent for the month of October, 1973 which was offered by the appellant first on October 1, 1973 and then on October 6, 1973. Furthermore, having no other alternative the appellant remitted the rent by postal money order which was refused and returned to him on November 5, 1973. The appellant deposited the rent with the House Rent Controller on November 18, 1973 and has been regularly depositing rent. The trial Court decreed the suit on February 14, 1975 on the ground of default and on the question of bonfire requirement; its finding was that it was concocted for the purposes of suit. 

 4. The High Court found that (1) the exhibit 1 was a deed of agreement for monthly tenancy and did not require to be registered under section 107 of the Transfer of Property Act and section 17 of the Registration Act, (2) exhibit 1 being a simple deed of agreement for a monthly tenancy it could be terminated on a month's notice by either side (3) the defendant failed to show that the tenancy agreement was for twenty four months, (4) the defendant is a defaulter within the meaning of section 18 (5) of the Premises Rent Control Ordinance, 1963. 

 1. That the 1st party will let out the Ground, first floor and Second floor of his gives if 	81/1, Kakril Road, which is a three storied building and of which the first party is the 16/- annas owner; at, a monthly rent of Tk. 1600/- (Taka sixteen hundred) only payable according to English Calendar month. The 2nd party has agreed to take the above mentioned entire three storied building at the stipulated rent of Tk. 1600/-(Taka sixteen hundred) only. It may be noted here that there is a store room in the 2nd floor and this store-room will be used only by the 1st party. The 2nd party will raise no demand for this room in future. 

 2. That an amount of Taka. 19,200/-(Taka nineteen thousand two hundred) only will be paid in advance by the 2nd party to the 1st party and out of that an amount of Tk. 800/-(Taka. eight hundred) only will be deducted every month towards payment of rent and in this way within a period of 24 (twenty four) months the entire advanced amount will be deducted and thereafter the 2nd party will pay rent at the rate of Tk. 1600/-(Taka. sixteen hundred) only per month to the 1st party. 

 3. That the rent will be payable within seven days of the current month according to English calendar month. 

 "Mr. T. H. Khan, learned Counsel for the petitioner, submits that the deed of agreement having contemplated that the advance of Tk. 19,200/- would be liquidated in course- of two years by adjustment of half of the monthly rental every month, the agreement for lease was for more than one year and as such the said deed was compulsorily registerable under the provisions of the Registration Act; and that the said deed of agreement being an unregistered document was inadmissible in evidence. Learned Counsel has further contended that the agreement for the tenancy having provided for the deposit of an advance of Tk. 19,200/- i.e. the rent for twelve months was violate of Section 20 of the Premises Rent Control Ordinance and as such was null and void. 

 It is the contention of the learned Counsel that under the provisions of the Rent Control Ordinance the petitioner could not be adjusted a defaulter and the agreement of the tenancy being inadmissible in evidence and also null and void according to law, the Courts below were wrong in relying upon the previsions of the said deed of agreement for their finding on the question of default. The learned Counsel has further argued that, in any view of the matter a large of unadjusted money as advance keying been in the hands of the respondent the Courts below were wrong in holding the petitioner a defaulter under the provisions of the Premises Rent Control Ordinance. "We think that the question raised merit consideration." 

 6. After referring to Clauses 1 and 2 of the agreement quoted above, the learned angel for the petitioner-submitted that they showed that the appellant took the premises at a monthly rent of Tk. 1600/- payable according to English Calendar month. Further, the appellant paid an amount of Tk. 19,260/- in advance to the respondents out of which an amount of Tk. 800/- would be deducted every month towards payment of rent and would pay an amount of Tk. 800/- per month in cash and in this way the entire amount advance will be deducted within a period of twenty four months. From Clause 2 of the agreement it would appear that the tenancy was created for a period of two years. Though in Clause 1 of the agreement it has been mentioned that the appellant was taking the premises at a monthly rent of Tk. 1600/- payable according to English Calendar month, Clause 2 of the agreement mentions the payment of an advance of Tk. 19,200/- out of which an amount of Tk. 800/- will be deducted every month towards payment of rent. After the advance will be deducted in this way within cried of twenty four months the appellant will pay rent ® Tk. 1600/-in cash every month. 

 7. According to the learned Counsel this shows that the agreement was vocative of the provisions of the Rent Control Ordinance, 963 and as such illegal and the appellant canto, therefore, be held to be a defaulter. 

 11. The learned Counsel referred to a few decisions where the distinction between the two terms, 'object' and 'consideration' has been considered. In Jaffar Meher Ali V. Budge Jute Mills Co. ILR 33 Calcutta 702, the interest of one Kasem Karim was assigned to the plaintiff. who, as an assignee, wanted to enforce his rights under the contract. The defendant contended that the assignment was made with the object of defeating the creditors of the assigner and, therefore, void against it. Sale J., in repelling the contention that the terms 'object' and 'consideration' did not mean two different things, but meant two different view of the same thing, or, in other words, the object of the agreement was the same as the consideration, expressed views as follows: 

 14. From the decision quoted above, it appears that some attempt has been made to show that the word object' in section 23 was not used in the same since as 'consideration.' The word 'object' means purpose or design. If the object or purpose of an agreement is unlawful, it would be unenforceable. Even conceding where the agreement does not show any object which may be described as unlawful, this, does not, however, remove the difficulty in the way of its being termed as unlawful within the meaning of section 23, if the agreement was for an unlawful consideration. For, section 23 also speaks of 'consideration.' In order, therefore, to determine whether an agreement is enforceable being a valid contract, the 'consideration' for which it has been made must also be shown to be lawful. Before proceeding to consider the lawfulness of the 'object' or 'consideration' of the agreement in question before us, it is necessary to refer to section 10 of the Premises Rent Control Ordinance, 1963, which provides as follows:- 

 "10.(a) Claim, receive or invite offers or ask for the payment of any premium, salami, fine or any other like sum in addition to the rent, or (b) except with the 	previous written consent of the Controller, claim or receive the payment of any sum exceeding one month's rent of such premises as rent in advance." 

 15. It is seen that Clause (a) of this section prohibits the acceptance of any sum of money over and above the rent payable by a tenant. This clause has also made illegal even any claim or invitation of an offer for the payment of such sum of money in the form of premium, salami or fine either when tenancy is being created or renewed, or during its continuance. Under Clause (b) no one is allowed to claim or receive a payment of more than one month's rent in advance. 

 16. According to Mr. Pal, Clause 10 of the agreement shows that a monthly tenancy has been created which is not dependent on the provisions of Clause 2 which mentioned the payment of Tk. 19,200/- as advance rent for twelve months, but the consideration for the creation of the tenancy is payment of a Monthly rent of Tk. 1600/- per month. He further submitted that the payment of Tk. 19,200/- as advance is not the consideration for which the agreement was concluded. Clause 2 of the agreement which stipulates the payment of an advance of tk. 19,200/ does not show the amount will be adjusted over a period of twenty four months against the payment of monthly rent. Mr. Pal further submitted that the provisions of Clauses 3, 13 and 14 of the agreement which mentions the requirement of monthly payment of rent and the determination of the tenancy on one months notice on either side have taken it out of the ambit of section 107 of the Transfer of Property Act, that is to say, it cannot be regarded as having created a lease for a period exceeding one year requiring registration under section 17(1) (d) of the Registration Act. Further, whether in the absence of the registration of the agreement, the document would be admissible in evidence or given effect to, is altogether a different matter. The legal consequences which flow from the absence of registration of the agreement are no doubt its inadmissibility as evidence to show that the agreement has created a lease for a period of two years. 

 The agreement to pay Tk. 19,200/- by way of advance rent was undoubtedly a part of the consideration of the transaction as defined in section 2(d) of the Contract Act. This contravenes the positive statutory mandate as provided in section 10(b) of the Premises Rent Control Ordinance, As regards the object of the transaction; the agreement does not appear to be free from doubt. 

 18. It was argued that the object of the agreement to create tenancy was not unlawful, but it can very well be said that the object was to realize a sum of Tk. 19,200/- by way of advance rent which is prohibited by law. 

 20. On the question of the agreement, the parties to the transaction seem to have contemplated a lease for at least two years on expiry of which the advanced amount would be liquadrated by adjustment towards the rent accruing during the said period. There is no term in the agreement providing for the refund of unadjusted amount of the money had and received by the respondents in case of earlier termination of the tenancy. Clause 2 of the agreement is clear enough to show that the parties intended that the tenancy subsists for more than two years. 

 21. In view of the unenforceability of the agreement the position is that the appellant is a monthly tenant who is liable to ejectment if he makes default in payment of rent as provided in Section 18(5) of the Premises Rent Control Ordinance. As the facts of the present case show, the respondent asserted that the appellant did not pay rent since October, 1973. On the other hand, according to the appellant, he offered rent of October, 1973 to the respondent who did not accept it and so he remitted the rent for the month of October by the money order dated November 1, 1973. In the written statement the appellant has stated that he offered the rent for the month of October on two dates, October 1, 1973 and October 6, 1973. 

 22. The provision of section 18(5) of the Premises Rent Control Act provides as follows:- 

 "18(5) No tenant shall be entitled to the benefit of this section in respect of any premises unless, he pays the rent due by him in respect of such premises to the full extent allowable by this Ordinance within the time fixed in the contract with his landlord or in the absence of such contract by the fifteenth day of the month next following that for 	which the lent is payable, or in the cases provided for in Section 19, unless the tenant has deposited such rent or any subsequent rent in respect of such premises as provided in that section together with in the case mentioned in clause (b) of sub-section (1) of that section the cost of transmission referred to in that clause within the time specified in that section. 

 Explanation-A. landlord shall not for the purposes of this subsection be deemed to have refused to accept any rent unless the rent is remitted within the period referred to above in this sub-section by postal money order to the address of the landlord and the rent so remitted is returned to the tenant by the pastel authorities as undelivered either on account of the landlord having refused to accept payment thereof for any other cause". 

 23. According to the aforesaid provisions, the tenant must pay the rent within the time fixed in the contract with his landlord or, in the absence of such contract by the fifteenth day of the month next following that for which the rent is payable. If the landlord refused to accept any rent sent within the aforesaid period as mentioned in the Explanation to section 18(5), the tenant is to deposit the rent as mentioned in section 19 of the Ordinance. 

 24. Since the respondent refused to accept the rent for the month of October which was sent by the appellant by money order on November 1, 1973 the latter deposited the rent for October November 20, 1973 and for the months of November and on December 14, 1973. The learned Counsel for the appellant submitted that as the appellant complied with the aforesaid provision of law it cannot be said that he made any default in payment of rent for October so as to be liable for ejectment, or even for any default in respect of the months of November and December. 

 25. Next, the learned Counsel submitted that until the entire amount of tk. 19,200/- taken by the respondents at the time of creating the tenancy was adjusted, the appellant could not be said to have defaulted in paying rent within the meaning of the aforesaid section. It cannot be denied Lilac there is considerable force in this argument. As long as the respondents had the unadjusted amount in their lands, they could nave adjusted it towards the payment of rent for the mouths of October, November and December. In view of the provisions of section 18(5) of the Ordinance which do not seem to have been contravened by appellant no default appears to have been made by him in paying the rent for the months of October, November and December, 1973.
